payload.task_text:
I need to put together an enrollment overview for all our Spring 2014 courses. Please look through the course catalog and find every course that has "Spring 2014" in its name (equivalently, course codes ending in "2014B"). For each of those courses, count how many students are enrolled (only counting StudentEnrollment type) and how many teachers.

Put everything into an Excel file called Spring2014_Enrollment.xlsx. The first sheet should be called "Enrollment" with columns Course_Name, Course_Code, Student_Count, Teacher_Count, and Student_Teacher_Ratio (students divided by teachers, rounded to 1 decimal, use 0 if there are no teachers). Sort this sheet by Student_Count from lowest to highest.

Add a second sheet called "Summary" with two columns Metric and Value. Include these rows: Total_Courses (how many Spring 2014 courses there are), Total_Students (sum of all students across courses), Avg_Students_Per_Course (rounded to the nearest whole number), Smallest_Course (the name of the course with the fewest students), and Largest_Course (the name of the course with the most students).

Also create a calendar event titled "Spring 2014 Enrollment Review" scheduled for March 14, 2026 from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM UTC.

Finally, send an email to registrar@university.edu with the subject "Spring 2014 Enrollment Summary" that includes the total number of courses, total students, and which course has the highest and lowest enrollment.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete this six-course workflow directly; do not dispatch sub-agents. Resolve the accessible task workspace dynamically and place Spring2014_Enrollment.xlsx there.

Call canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true), retain every and only course whose full name contains Spring 2014 or whose code ends in 2014B, and freeze its literal ID/code/name. For each retained course, issue StudentEnrollment and TeacherEnrollment canvas_get_course_grades calls together in one native-parallel response with page=1 and per_page=1. Use pagination.total_count for the two counts; do not fetch enrollment rows. Reject identity mismatches or duplicate/missing Spring courses.

Compute a single canonical table with {course_name, course_code, student_count, teacher_count, student_teacher_ratio}, sorted by student_count ascending and course_code ascending for ties. Compute all Summary metrics once from that table, including deterministic smallest/largest course names, and freeze the exact email facts.

The main agent is the sole writer of Spring2014_Enrollment.xlsx. Create exactly Enrollment and Summary with the task's exact headers, literal values and rounding, then read both populated ranges back from the resolved path. Once the canonical payload is frozen, run the workbook branch, the exact calendar lookup for Spring 2014 Enrollment Review at 2026-03-14T14:00:00Z--15:00:00Z, and the exact Sent-mail lookup for registrar@university.edu / Spring 2014 Enrollment Summary natively in parallel where possible. Create only a missing exact event, leaving attendees empty and using the task's UTC times. Send only a missing exact-recipient/subject message and include the canonical course count, total students, largest course and smallest course. Read the event and message back; do not retry ambiguous creates.

nodes.text:
I need to build an enrollment overview for all Spring 2014 courses in Canvas. Your job is to gather the raw data and report it back to me. Do NOT write any files or send anything — just read Canvas and report.

Steps:
1. Explore the Canvas course catalog. List courses (try canvas_list_courses, canvas_list_account_courses with a suitable account_id, and/or canvas_get_dashboard_cards to discover courses). Identify every course whose name contains "Spring 2014" OR whose course code ends with "2014B". These are the target courses. There may be a large catalog — use search_term filters where available to find them efficiently (e.g., search for "2014" or "Spring").
2. For each target course, get its exact course name and course code (sis_course_id or course_code).
3. For each target course, count the number of enrollments of type StudentEnrollment (active/whatever states exist — count all enrollments with type StudentEnrollment; note if any are non-active and include them in your count) and the number of enrollments of type TeacherEnrollment. Use canvas_get_course_grades with type[] filters (["StudentEnrollment"], ["TeacherEnrollment"]) to get counts — page through with per_page=100 and pagination.has_more if needed. You can also cross-check with canvas_list_course_users if helpful.

Deliverable: Report back a clear table listing, for EVERY Spring 2014 course: Course_Name (exact), Course_Code (exact), Student_Count (number of StudentEnrollment enrollments), Teacher_Count (number of TeacherEnrollment enrollments). Also state the total number of Spring 2014 courses found. If any course is ambiguous (name contains Spring 2014 but code doesn't end in 2014B, or vice versa), list it and include it only if it clearly matches "Spring 2014" in the name per the primary criterion.
Gather Spring 2014 enrollment data

Create an Excel workbook at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-enrollment-overview-excel-email/workspace/Spring2014_Enrollment.xlsx using the excel MCP tools (mcp__excel__*). 

The workbook must have exactly two sheets with the following content. Use mcp__excel__create_workbook to create the file, then write data with mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel, and rename the default sheet if needed.

SHEET 1 — name it exactly "Enrollment". Columns and rows (row 1 = headers):
Headers: Course_Name | Course_Code | Student_Count | Teacher_Count | Student_Teacher_Ratio

Data rows (already sorted by Student_Count ascending — write in this exact order):
1. Environmental Economics & Ethics (Spring 2014) | EEE-2014B | 694 | 1 | 694.0
2. Global Governance & Geopolitics (Spring 2014) | GGG-2014B | 833 | 1 | 833.0
3. Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014) | DDD-2014B | 1228 | 3 | 409.3
4. Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014) | FFF-2014B | 1500 | 2 | 750.0
5. Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014) | BBB-2014B | 1613 | 0 | 0
6. Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014) | CCC-2014B | 1936 | 2 | 968.0

Note: Student_Teacher_Ratio = Student_Count / Teacher_Count rounded to 1 decimal, and 0 when Teacher_Count is 0 (as in row 5). The values above are pre-computed; write them exactly as shown (numeric values, not strings).

SHEET 2 — name it exactly "Summary". Columns Metric | Value with these rows (row 1 = headers):
Metric | Value
Total_Courses | 6
Total_Students | 7804
Avg_Students_Per_Course | 1301
Smallest_Course | Environmental Economics & Ethics (Spring 2014)
Largest_Course | Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014)

(Total_Students = 694+833+1228+1500+1613+1936 = 7804. Avg = 7804/6 = 1300.67 → rounded to nearest whole number = 1301. Smallest course = fewest students = EEE with 694. Largest = most students = CCC with 1936.)

After writing, verify by reading back the workbook (mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata and/or mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel on both sheets) and confirm the two sheet names are exactly "Enrollment" and "Summary" (delete any default extra sheet if the workbook came with one, e.g. "Sheet1", so the workbook contains ONLY these two sheets).

Deliverable: Report the absolute file path, the confirmed sheet names, and confirm the data matches the spec exactly.
Build Spring2014_Enrollment.xlsx

Perform two external actions using your tools:

1. GOOGLE CALENDAR EVENT: Create a calendar event with mcp__google_calendar__create_event:
- summary: "Spring 2014 Enrollment Review"
- start: dateTime "2026-03-14T14:00:00" with timeZone "UTC"
- end: dateTime "2026-03-14T15:00:00" with timeZone "UTC"
No attendees needed. Report the event ID returned.

2. EMAIL: Send an email with mcp__emails__send_email:
- to: registrar@university.edu
- subject: "Spring 2014 Enrollment Summary"
- body: A professional plain-text summary that includes: total number of Spring 2014 courses (6), total number of students across all courses (7804), the course with the highest enrollment (Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014) with 1936 students), and the course with the lowest enrollment (Environmental Economics & Ethics (Spring 2014) with 694 students). Write a clear, complete body — do not truncate the data.

Deliverable: Report the calendar event ID and confirmation that the email was sent (including recipient, subject), or any error returned.
Create calendar event and send email
